title: BriefingPack Frontmatter
description: Validates the YAML frontmatter of an i-SASE BriefingPack artifact. A BriefingPack defines a mission with its loop script, mentor scripts, and operational metadata.

schema.description: Schema identifier for the BriefingPack artifact type.

id.description: Unique 12-character hex identifier for the BriefingPack.

slug.description: Human-readable short name (2-4 words, lowercase, hyphens). Used in directory name and display.

mission.description: Human-readable description of the mission objective.

created.description: ISO-8601 date when the BriefingPack was created.

author.description: Authors or originators of the BriefingPack.

status.description: Current lifecycle status. Parent BPs with children have their status derived automatically. 'stale' = work was completed/reviewed but a BP it depends on has been revised since; reassessment required.

rigor.description: Rigor level governing how strictly the SASE loop enforces gates and reviews.

depends-on.description: IDs of sibling BPs that must be completed before this BP can start.

execution-order.description: Ordered execution plan for children. Strings = sequential, arrays = parallel groups.

agent-id.description: ID of agent that claimed this BP

claimed.description: When the agent claimed this BP

approver.description: Team member who approved this BP as ready

loop-script.description: File path to the LoopScript YAML that defines the phase sequence for this mission.

mentor-scripts.description: List of file paths to MentorScript documents that apply to this mission.

constraints.description: Human-authored binding constraints: business rules, tech mandates, performance budgets

approach.description: Implementation strategy. Agent-proposed or human-authored. Agent may deviate with justification.

revision.description: Revision number of this BP. Incremented on each revise transition.

revision-log.description: Audit trail of previous revisions. Each entry records a completed execution cycle.

date.description: ISO date of completion or revision

mrp.description: MRP ID produced for this revision

vcr.description: VCR ID that reviewed this revision

outcome.description: How this revision concluded. 'confirmed-valid' = a stale BP was reassessed and its prior work was confirmed despite an upstream revision.

revision-reason.description: Why this revision was superseded ('revised' outcomes), or the confirmation note ('confirmed-valid' outcomes).

re-execution-scope.description: When a BP is revised, this field narrows the scope for the next agent. Optional — if absent, the agent re-executes everything.

preserve-artifacts.description: Artifacts from previous revision that remain valid and should not be regenerated

re-verify-artifacts.description: Artifacts that must be fixed and re-verified

stale-because.description: Records why this BP is currently in 'stale' status. One entry per upstream BP revision that has not yet been reassessed. Cleared when the BP is confirmed-valid or revised.

source-bp.description: Hash of the upstream BP whose revision triggered this flag.

source-revision.description: The revision number the upstream BP transitioned to when it triggered this flag.

revision-reason.description: The reason the upstream BP was revised (copied from its revision-log).

flagged-at.description: When this BP was flagged stale.

previous-status.description: Status this BP held before being flagged. Restored on confirm-valid.

artifacts.description: Declared artifact inputs and outputs for traceability. Lists files/directories this BP consumes (input) or produces (output).

path.description: Relative path from project root to the artifact file or directory.

direction.description: Whether this BP consumes (input) or produces (output) the artifact.

ac.description: Reference to the Acceptance Criterion that requires this artifact (e.g. AC-1). Only meaningful for outputs.

verify-command.description: Shell command that proves this output artifact is valid. Executed from project root. Must exit 0. Only meaningful for output artifacts.
